zh.summary: 依工作目的分組與命名資訊，再用標題、順序與動作層次幫使用者找到當下要做的事。
objectives: 區分資訊架構、導覽元件與視覺優先序。
依收件任務排列輸入、檢查、結果與次要資訊。
檢查手機閱讀順序及非顏色提示是否仍傳達相同意思。

readingGuide.goal: 區分資訊架構、導覽元件與視覺優先序。
readingGuide.startingPoint: 文字編輯器與四狀態收件草圖；只使用合成欄位名稱與資料。
readingGuide.route: 先看情境與原理，再比較例子，最後擴寫 wireframe-notes.md 並用檢核題自查。
readingGuide.output: wireframe-notes.md 具有內容清單、群組、主要動作及手機閱讀順序。

sections.heading: 資訊架構與視覺優先序：讓使用者知道該做什麼
paragraphs: 這一課最重要的觀念是：好的介面，不只是把資訊放在畫面上，而是讓使用者知道資訊在哪裡、現在應該注意什麼，以及下一步可以做什麼。
假設你走進一家醫院，要完成掛號、看診、批價與領藥。
醫院可能設備先進、裝潢漂亮，但如果掛號櫃檯沒有清楚標示、領藥窗口與繳費窗口混在一起、指示牌充滿看不懂的縮寫，你仍然會感到困惑。
軟體介面也是如此。
設計介面之前，必須先解決三個不同的問題：

blocks.caption: 三種觀念解決不同問題
rows: 資訊架構（IA）
東西應該如何分類、命名與建立關係
我需要的東西在哪裡？
導覽（Navigation）
用什麼方式讓人找到它
我要怎麼過去？
視覺優先序（Visual Hierarchy）
哪些東西應該先被注意到
現在應該先看什麼、做什麼？

paragraphs: 這三者彼此相關，但不能混為一談。教材也特別強調：應該先整理資訊關係，再決定側邊欄、分頁、按鈕等外觀。

sections.heading: 一、資訊架構（IA）：先把東西整理好，再談怎麼展示
paragraphs: 先從使用者能理解的分類與名稱開始。

blocks.heading: 超市與學生服務分類
paragraphs: 想像一家大型超市。
沒有合理分類
牛奶、洗衣精、餅乾與電池混在一起，需要不斷尋找。
依顧客需求分類
生鮮、飲料、清潔用品各有區域，顧客可以預測商品位置。
真正改善購物效率的，不只是把貨架換新或改善燈光，而是建立合理的商品分類與擺放關係。
網站也一樣。
假設我們要設計一個大學的學生服務網站，裡面有以下功能：
選課、繳學費、獎學金申請、成績查詢、停車證申請、教授研究計畫、教室借用、畢業離校。
一種分類方法是按照學校行政單位：

- 教務處
- 學務處
- 總務處
- 研究發展處
這是按照組織內部架構分類。
另一種方法是按照學生希望完成的工作：

- 課業與成績
- 學費與獎助
- 校園生活與設施
- 研究與畢業
這是按照使用者的任務分類。
哪種一定比較好？
不一定。假如使用者主要是行政職員，按照權責單位分類可能合理；但如果服務對象是第一次入學的學生，按照任務分類通常是更值得測試的起點。
因此，IA 有一個很重要的設計原則：
資訊應該盡量依照使用者理解世界的方式組織，而不是直接照搬開發團隊或行政組織的內部分工。

blocks.heading: IA 不等於網站地圖
paragraphs: 以下包含關係區分工作範圍與結構產物。

blocks.caption: 圖 1｜IA 工作、網站結構與網站地圖的包含關係
blocks.description: 依 Nielsen Norman Group 的原圖重新繪製。巢狀邊界表示包含，不表示執行順序；網站地圖只呈現部分結構。

items.title: 資訊架構工作
items.body:
內容盤點
內容品質檢查
IA 使用者研究
分類與標籤

items.title: 規劃網站結構
items.body: 建立內容組織與層級

items.title: 網站地圖
items.body: 以圖呈現網站結構

paragraphs: Nielsen Norman Group 的示意圖說明：網站地圖（Sitemap）只是在呈現網站結構，而網站結構規劃又只是資訊架構工作的一部分。
IA 還包括內容盤點、內容品質檢查、使用者研究、分類命名等。
IA 是整理整座城市的規劃；Sitemap 是畫出城市的區域地圖；Navigation 是道路與路標。
所以，當網站有資訊混亂的問題時，不能只靠新增一個漂亮的選單來解決。

sections.heading: 二、導覽（Navigation）：讓人知道怎麼找到東西
paragraphs: 如果資訊架構是超市的商品分類，導覽就是超市裡的指示牌與通道。
例如，電商網站把商品分為「服飾、家電、食品、居家用品」。這是資訊架構。
但消費者要怎麼找到這些分類？
可以透過頂端選單、側邊欄、搜尋框、商品篩選器，或首頁的分類入口。
這些都是導覽元件。

blocks.caption: 圖 2｜電商網站地圖：首頁與四個平行分支
blocks.description: 參考隨文 UsabilityHub 電商網站地圖重繪。首頁包含商品、購物車、帳戶與其他頁面。線與縮排表示父子隸屬；分類／支援／探索另有下一層，不表示購物步驟。

items.title: 首頁
items.body: 商品、購物車、帳戶、其他頁面

items.title: 商品
items.body:
分類
  精選
  系列
  出清
商品詳情
商品比較

items.title: 購物車
items.body:
訂單摘要
配送方式
付款方式
配送

items.title: 帳戶
items.body:
個人資料
付款方式
密碼
儲存的地址
訂單紀錄
禮物卡

items.title: 其他頁面
items.body:
支援
  分類 1
  分類 2
探索
  圖庫
  部落格
  社群
關於我們

paragraphs: 網站地圖描述的是內容之間的關係。真正使用網站時，我們不一定會看到整張地圖，而是透過選單、搜尋或連結來移動。

blocks.heading: 為什麼不能一開始就決定要做側邊欄？
paragraphs: 假設你要製作一個線上報名系統，只需要三步：

1. 輸入個人資料。
2. 確認報名資訊。
3. 完成報名。
這時候，做成一個簡單的三步驟介面可能就足夠了。
如果為了看起來像專業系統，硬是加入左側選單、上方分頁、右側工具列，反而讓操作更複雜。
但如果是一個有數百項功能的企業管理平台，就可能需要側邊欄、搜尋功能與多層導覽。
導覽形式應該由資訊複雜度、使用者任務和使用情境決定，而不是由設計師喜歡哪種外觀決定。

sections.heading: 三、視覺優先序（Visual Hierarchy）：讓重要的事情先被看見
paragraphs: 想像飛機駕駛艙。
飛行員面前有許多儀表，但是正在飛行時，飛行高度、速度、警告訊息等資料的重要程度，與座椅調整設定完全不同。
如果所有資訊都用一樣大的字體、一樣鮮豔的顏色呈現，就會增加辨認重點的困難。
介面設計也有同樣的問題。
視覺優先序，就是透過大小、位置、間距、對比與分組，讓使用者在視覺上更容易分辨資訊的重要程度。
Nielsen Norman Group 將視覺優先序列為重要的視覺設計原則之一。

blocks.heading: 看看兩種不同的資訊安排
paragraphs: 先比較兩個畫面如何呈現狀態、問題與下一步。

blocks.caption: 圖 3｜相近功能，兩種資訊安排
blocks.description: A／B 是平行比較，沒有先後箭頭。此為說明性草圖，沒有可操作功能，也尚未經使用者測試。

items.title: 安排 A｜所有事情都很重要
items.body:
管理系統

進階設定
下載報告
查看結果
開始檢查

狀態：INVALID

資料、說明、紀錄、診斷、輸出混在一起。

問題：使用者不清楚現在該做哪件事。

items.title: 安排 B｜依照工作任務呈現
items.body:
申請資料檢查

請確認三項必要資料。

申請編號：A1024
申請人代號：P008
文件類型：未填寫

尚缺少文件類型

補填文件類型

改善方向：錯誤、修正方式與下一個動作有清楚關聯。

paragraphs: 以上是說明性草圖，不是經過使用者測試的正式設計，也沒有可操作功能。
兩種安排包含類似的功能，但第二種讓使用者更容易回答三個問題：

- 我現在處於什麼狀態？
- 有什麼問題需要處理？
- 下一步應該做什麼？
這就是視覺優先序真正要達到的目的。

blocks.heading: 視覺優先序的五種常用方法
paragraphs: 下表以五個面向整理可檢查的視覺安排。

blocks.caption: 視覺優先序的五種常用方法
rows: 大小（Scale）
更重要的標題通常更醒目
頁面主標題大於補充說明
位置（Position）
把當前需要的資訊放在容易發現的地方
付款總額靠近確認付款動作
對比（Contrast）
用視覺差異區分不同重要性
主要操作與次要操作不同
間距（Spacing）
相關資訊靠近，不相關的適度分開
訂單金額與付款按鈕形成群組
分組（Grouping）
相同任務的資訊放在一起
病人資料與檢查結果分為兩區

paragraphs: 不是所有重要資訊都要放大、加粗或使用鮮豔顏色。
如果畫面上每個按鈕都很醒目，使用者仍然不知道哪一個最重要。
好的視覺優先序，是讓不同資訊有適當的層次。

sections.heading: 四、主要動作（Primary Action）：不同狀態下，最重要的事會改變
paragraphs: 想像你在機場使用自助報到機。
尚未輸入訂位資料時，主要動作是「查詢訂位」。
找到訂位後，主要動作可能變成「確認航班與旅客」。
完成報到後，才出現「列印登機證」。
系統不能在任何狀態下，都把「查詢訂位」「確認報到」「列印登機證」三個按鈕放得一樣顯眼，卻不解釋各自的使用條件。
因為操作有先後關係。

blocks.caption: 圖 4｜資料完整性檢查：狀態與主要動作
blocks.description: 四列對照可能的狀態及動作，不是保證依序發生的四步。完整性檢查通過不代表正式審核或核准。

items.title: 尚未檢查
items.body: 使用者需要確認輸入內容，主要動作是「檢查資料」。

items.title: 檢查中
items.body: 顯示檢查進度，避免重複提交，並說明目前正在處理。

items.title: 發現缺件
items.body: 明確指出缺少什麼，主要動作改為「補填資料並重新檢查」。

items.title: 完整性檢查通過
items.body: 顯示當次檢查結果，必要時才提供「預覽」與「匯出報告」。

paragraphs: 這是示範用的四狀態設計。完整性檢查通過不代表正式審核或核准。
這裡的關鍵是：主要動作跟隨使用者目前的狀態改變，而不是讓使用者自己從許多按鈕中猜測。
不過，也不能為了介面簡潔，就把重要錯誤隱藏。
例如，醫療系統顯示某項檢驗仍缺資料，即使這種情況不常發生，也應該明確告知，而不是把它藏到「進階設定」。

sections.heading: 五、手機與電腦：畫面可以改變，但資訊的意思不能改變
paragraphs: Responsive Design（響應式設計）：同一套介面隨著螢幕尺寸與操作方式改變呈現。
假設電腦版把「資料輸入」放左邊、「注意事項」放右邊。
在手機上，左右並排通常會改成上下排列。
但如果注意事項說「請先確認檢查條件，才能送出」，那麼重新排列後，注意事項就不應該落在使用者已完成送出操作之後。

blocks.caption: 圖 5｜版型改變，閱讀順序保持一致
blocks.description: 桌面把 2／3 並排，手機改成上下排列；兩者都依 1→2→3→4 閱讀。數字表示有意義的資訊順序，不是四次實際提交。

items.title: 桌面版
items.body:
1. 任務與注意事項
2. 輸入資料
3. 輸入說明
4. 檢查與結果

items.title: 手機版
items.body:
1. 任務與注意事項
2. 輸入資料
3. 輸入說明
4. 檢查與結果

paragraphs: 示意：視覺位置可以改變，但有意義的資訊先後關係必須保留。
W3C 的 WCAG 2.2「Meaningful Sequence」（有意義的順序）規定：當內容順序會影響理解時，程式必須能判定合理的閱讀順序。
並不是所有獨立卡片都只能有一種排列方式；重要的是，不要讓重新排版破壞原本的意思。

blocks.heading: 還有一個常被忽略的細節：欄位名稱
paragraphs: 假設一個輸入框裡寫：
`請輸入申請編號`
這稱為 Placeholder（輸入提示文字）。
問題在於使用者開始輸入後，提示通常就消失了。
比較可靠的做法是讓「申請編號」成為持續可見的 Label（欄位標籤），再另外提供格式範例。
而且在程式中，還需要讓這個標籤與輸入控制項正確關聯，讓螢幕閱讀器等輔助科技能辨認。
所以，介面設計不只是讓眼睛看起來舒服，也要讓不同能力、不同裝置的使用者都能正確理解與操作。

sections.heading: 六、從不同行業看，怎麼應用這些觀念
paragraphs: 以下案例分別整理資訊關係與當前應注意的重點。

blocks.caption: 六種行業的資訊架構與優先序
headers: 視覺優先序應該突出什麼
rows: 醫療
病人資料、檢驗、用藥、處置如何分組
當前需要處理的臨床資訊與重要警示
電商
商品如何分類與篩選
商品價格、規格、庫存、購買動作
銀行
帳戶、轉帳、投資與貸款如何組織
金額、收款對象、交易確認與風險提醒
製造業
設備、工單、維修與品質資料如何組織
異常設備、待處理工單、停機警報
教育
課程、教材、作業、測驗如何分組
目前進度、下一個學習任務、待完成事項
政府服務
申請、查詢、補件、進度追蹤如何分類
目前案件狀態、期限與下一步處理方式

paragraphs: 這些例子有共同原則，但沒有一種固定排版能適用所有產業。
例如醫療儀表板與電商網站，都需要視覺優先序，但兩者對於錯誤提醒、資訊密度及操作限制的要求可能完全不同。

sections.heading: 七、真正要設計一個介面，應該如何開始？
paragraphs: 我建議把本課觀念轉成一套可以反覆使用的設計流程。

blocks.caption: 圖 6｜從使用者任務到可測試介面
blocks.description: 箭頭表示本課建議的設計工作順序；第五步包含驗證，不代表線框稿已通過真實使用者驗收。

items.title: 定義使用者與工作任務
items.body: 誰來使用？想完成什麼？

items.title: 盤點所有內容與功能
items.body: 需要哪些資料、按鈕、錯誤與結果？

items.title: 建立 IA：分類、命名與關係
items.body: 哪些資訊應該放在一起？

items.title: 定義狀態、導覽與視覺優先序
items.body: 每個狀態下，該先看什麼、做什麼？

items.title: 畫 Wireframe（線框稿）並驗證
items.body: 檢查桌面、手機、鍵盤及真實工作任務。

paragraphs: 其中，Wireframe 就是先用簡單的方框、文字和排列方式，畫出介面如何運作。暫時不需要處理精緻的圖示、配色與動畫。
如果要讓這套流程更有科學依據，還可以使用兩種研究方法：
Card Sorting（卡片分類法）：把功能名稱寫成卡片，請使用者依照自己的理解分組。目的是發現使用者心中可能的分類方式。
Tree Testing（樹狀結構測試）：先建立分類結構，再請使用者完成尋找任務，例如「請找到停車證申請」。觀察他們能否在不依賴美觀版面的情況下找到正確位置。
前者用來探索分類方式，後者用來評估已建立的架構。

blocks.heading: 將成果記錄成 wireframe-notes.md
paragraphs: 以下是一個可直接用在練習專案的簡化模板：
blocks.code:
# M04-03 畫面資訊與線框規劃

## 1. 使用者與任務
使用者：案件承辦人
目標：檢查三項必要資料是否完整

## 2. 內容清單
- 申請編號
- 申請人代號
- 文件類型
- 必填說明
- 檢查動作
- 缺漏與修正方式
- 當次檢查結果
- 預覽與匯出

## 3. 資訊分組
- 任務與限制
- 資料輸入
- 檢查動作與結果
- 次要說明及診斷

## 4. 主要動作
- 未檢查：檢查資料
- 檢查中：顯示處理狀態
- 缺件：補填並重新檢查
- 完整：預覽、匯出當次結果

## 5. 閱讀順序
任務 → 必要資料 → 檢查 → 結果

## 6. 待驗證事項
- 使用者能理解分類與欄位名稱嗎？
- 錯誤是否有文字說明及修正方法？
- 手機閱讀順序是否合理？
- 鍵盤能否依合理順序操作？
- Label 是否與輸入控制項正確關聯？

paragraphs: 中英頁共用上方原始專案模板；英文版另附六節內容的英文閱讀說明。
這樣做的好處是，你還沒有花時間寫前端程式，就已經把內容、流程、狀態與驗證條件整理出來。
之後交給人類工程師或 AI Coding Agent 實作，也比較容易明確溝通需求。

sections.heading: 八、本課最容易犯的五個錯誤
paragraphs: 用以下五種情況檢查候選介面。

1. 先畫漂亮畫面，再思考使用者需求。 可能出現視覺好看但工作流程不合理的介面。
2. 把資訊架構誤認成選單設計。 選單只是資訊架構的一種呈現方式。
3. 所有按鈕都同樣醒目。 缺乏明確的主要動作，增加判斷負擔。
4. 只靠顏色表示錯誤。 應以文字說明問題及修正方式，而不是只有紅色提示。
5. 只測試電腦的視覺排版。 忽略手機、鍵盤、螢幕閱讀器與實際操作順序。

sections.heading: 九、理解檢核：你是否真的掌握 M04-03？
paragraphs: 三題自我檢核列在下方「理解檢核」。先自行選擇，再展開參考解析；此頁不送出或保存答案。
本課最重要的一句話：先決定資訊應該如何組織，再決定使用者如何找到它，最後才決定如何透過視覺引導注意力與操作。
下一步可以接續 M04-04 的 Wireframe，把本課的分類、狀態與主要動作轉成具體線框稿。

exercise.environment: 文字編輯器與四狀態收件草圖；只使用合成欄位名稱與資料。
steps: 盤點必要欄位、動作、狀態、範例與診斷資訊，為每項指定用途與群組。
為未檢查、缺件、完成各選主要動作，寫出不能被隱藏的資訊。
用紙筆排出桌面與手機版本，線性讀出標題、欄位、結果與動作，記錄一項需要實作驗證的順序問題。
exercise.expected: wireframe-notes.md 具有內容清單、群組、主要動作及手機閱讀順序。
exercise.check: 名稱可理解，錯誤不只靠顏色或位置；能說明分組與導覽外觀的差異。
exercise.cleanup: 保留候選與待驗標記；不把個人偏好的位置或配色寫成普遍驗證結論。

en.summary: Group and name information around work goals, then use headings, order and action hierarchy to help users find what matters now.
objectives: Distinguish information architecture, navigation components and visual hierarchy.
Arrange input, checking, results and secondary information around the intake task.
Check that mobile reading order and non-color cues retain the same meaning.

readingGuide.goal: Distinguish information architecture, navigation components and visual hierarchy.
readingGuide.startingPoint: A text editor and four-state intake sketches, using synthetic field names and data only.
readingGuide.route: Read the situation and principles, compare examples, then expand wireframe-notes.md and use the checks to review your understanding.

sections.heading: Information architecture and visual hierarchy: help users know what to do
paragraphs: A useful interface helps people find information, recognize what needs attention now, and identify their next action.
Imagine visiting a hospital to register, see a clinician, pay and collect medication.

The hospital may have advanced equipment and attractive interiors. Yet an unmarked registration desk, confusing payment and pharmacy windows, or signs full of unfamiliar abbreviations can still leave you lost.
Software interfaces raise the same problem.
Before designing the screen, distinguish three questions:

blocks.caption: Three concepts address different questions
rows: Information architecture (IA)
Classify and name things, and define their relationships
Where is what I need?
Navigation
Provide ways to reach those things
How do I get there?
Visual hierarchy
Make different levels of importance perceptible
What should I notice and do first?

paragraphs: These concepts interact but describe different decisions. Organize information relationships before choosing sidebars, tabs and buttons.

sections.heading: 1. Information architecture: organize before presenting
paragraphs: Begin with categories and names that the intended users can understand.

blocks.heading: Supermarket and student-service categories
paragraphs: Imagine a large supermarket.
Without useful categories
Milk, laundry detergent, cookies and batteries are mixed together, making shoppers search repeatedly.
Group goods around shoppers’ needs
Fresh food, drinks and cleaning products occupy recognizable areas. Shoppers can predict where to look.
New shelving and better lighting alone do not establish these relationships. A useful product classification and placement scheme does.
The same reasoning applies to a website.
Suppose a university student-service site offers these functions:
Course registration, tuition payment, scholarship applications, grade lookup, parking permits, faculty research projects, classroom reservations and graduation clearance.
One organization follows the university's administrative units:

- Academic Affairs
- Student Affairs
- General Affairs
- Research and Development
This reflects the institution's internal organization.
Another organization follows the work students want to complete:

- Courses and grades
- Tuition and financial support
- Campus life and facilities
- Research and graduation
This reflects users' tasks.
Which is always better?
Neither is universally better. Grouping by responsible office may suit administrative staff. For new students, task-based categories are usually a useful starting hypothesis to test.
An IA principle follows:
Organize information around users' understanding of the domain. Avoid adopting the team's or institution's internal divisions without checking whether those divisions help the intended users.

blocks.heading: IA is broader than a sitemap
paragraphs: The nested regions distinguish the broader practice from its structural artifact.

blocks.caption: Figure 1 | IA practice contains structure planning and sitemaps
blocks.description: Redrawn from the Nielsen Norman Group reference. Nested boundaries mean inclusion, not execution order; a sitemap represents part of the structure.

items.title: Information architecture activities
items.body:
Content inventory
Content audit
IA user research
Taxonomies and tags

items.title: Plan website structure
items.body: Establish content organization and hierarchy

items.title: Sitemap
items.body: Visualize the website structure

paragraphs: Nielsen Norman Group's diagram places the sitemap inside website-structure planning, which is itself part of the broader practice of information architecture.
IA also covers content inventory, content quality audits, user research, classification and naming.
Think of IA as planning a city, a sitemap as a map of its districts, and navigation as roads and signs.
A more attractive menu alone cannot resolve poorly organized information.

sections.heading: 2. Navigation: help people reach information
paragraphs: If information architecture is the supermarket's classification of goods, navigation is its signs and aisles.
For example, an ecommerce site may classify products into clothing, appliances, food and home goods. That classification is part of its IA.
How do customers reach those categories?
They might use a top menu, sidebar, search field, product filters or category links on the homepage.
These are navigation components.

blocks.caption: Figure 2 | Ecommerce sitemap: homepage and four parallel branches
blocks.description: Redrawn from the supplied UsabilityHub ecommerce sitemap. The homepage has Products, Cart, Account and Other pages branches. Lines and indentation mean parent–child relationships. Categories, Support and Explore contain another level; this is not a checkout sequence.

items.title: Homepage
items.body: Products, Cart, Account, Other pages

items.title: Products
items.body:
Categories
  Featured
  Collections
  Clearance
Product details
Compare products

items.title: Cart
items.body:
Order summary
Shipping method
Payment method
Shipping

items.title: Account
items.body:
Profile
Payment methods
Password
Saved addresses
Order history
Gift cards

items.title: Other pages
items.body:
Support
  Category 1
  Category 2
Explore
  Gallery
  Blog
  Community
About us

paragraphs: A sitemap describes relationships among content. People using the site usually move through menus, search and links rather than inspecting the complete map.

blocks.heading: Why not choose a sidebar first?
paragraphs: Suppose an online registration service only needs three steps:

1. Enter personal details.
2. Confirm registration information.
3. Complete registration.
A simple three-step interface may be enough.
Adding a left menu, top tabs and a right toolbar just to make the service look professional can make the task harder.
An enterprise platform with hundreds of functions, however, may need a sidebar, search and multiple navigation levels.
Choose navigation forms according to information complexity, user tasks and context of use.

sections.heading: 3. Visual hierarchy: make important information noticeable
paragraphs: Imagine an aircraft cockpit.
During flight, altitude, speed and warnings have a different immediate importance from seat-adjustment settings.
Giving every item equally large text and equally vivid colors makes the priorities harder to distinguish.
Interfaces have the same issue.
Visual hierarchy uses size, position, spacing, contrast and grouping to help users distinguish levels of importance.
Nielsen Norman Group includes visual hierarchy among its visual-design principles.

blocks.heading: Compare two information arrangements
paragraphs: Compare how the two screens present state, problems and the next action.

blocks.caption: Figure 3 | Similar functions, two information arrangements
blocks.description: A and B are alternatives with no sequence arrows. These are explanatory sketches, with no working controls or user-test evidence.

items.title: Arrangement A | Everything is important
items.body:
Management system

Advanced settings
Download report
View results
Start check

Status: INVALID

Data, instructions, records, diagnostics and output are mixed together.

Problem: users cannot identify what to do now.

items.title: Arrangement B | Organize around the task
items.body:
Application-data check

Confirm the three required fields.

Application ID: A1024
Applicant code: P008
Document type: not entered

Document type is missing

Enter document type

Improvement: the error, correction and next action have a clear relationship.

paragraphs: These are explanatory sketches, with no working controls or evidence from user testing.
The two arrangements contain similar functions, but the second helps users answer three questions:

- What state am I in now?
- What problem needs attention?
- What should I do next?
Visual hierarchy supports those judgments.

blocks.heading: Five common ways to establish visual hierarchy
paragraphs: The table organizes five aspects of a candidate visual arrangement.

blocks.caption: Five ways to establish visual hierarchy
rows: Scale
Make more important headings easier to notice
A page title is larger than supporting information
Position
Place information needed now where people can find it
Put the payment total near the confirmation action
Contrast
Use visual differences to distinguish importance
Distinguish primary and secondary actions
Spacing
Keep related information close and separate unrelated content
Group the order amount with the payment button
Grouping
Place information serving the same task together
Separate patient details from test results

paragraphs: Not every important item needs larger type, bold text or vivid color.
If every button stands out equally, users still have to guess which action matters now.
A useful hierarchy provides appropriate differences among information levels.

sections.heading: 4. Primary action: the priority changes with state
paragraphs: Consider an airport self-service check-in kiosk.
Before a reservation has been entered, the primary action is to look up the booking.
After the booking is found, it may become confirming the flight and travelers.
Only after check-in is complete does printing a boarding pass become appropriate.
Displaying booking lookup, check-in confirmation and boarding-pass printing with equal emphasis in every state, without their preconditions, conceals the order of the work.
These actions have dependencies.

blocks.caption: Figure 4 | Completeness-check states and primary actions
blocks.description: The four rows associate possible states with actions, not four steps that must always occur. Completeness does not establish formal review or approval.

items.title: Not checked
items.body: Confirm the inputs. The primary action is Check data.

items.title: Checking
items.body: Show progress, prevent duplicate submission and explain that processing is underway.

items.title: Missing information
items.body: Identify the omission. The primary action becomes Fill in missing data and check again.

items.title: Completeness check passed
items.body: Show the result for this check. Offer Preview and Export report when needed.

paragraphs: This example distinguishes four states. Passing a completeness check does not establish formal review or approval.
The primary action follows the user's current state, reducing the need to guess among unrelated buttons.
Keep important errors visible when simplifying an interface.
For example, if a medical system lacks information required for a test, show that omission explicitly even if it occurs infrequently. Hiding it in advanced settings makes it harder to resolve.

sections.heading: 5. Mobile and desktop: preserve meaning as layout changes
paragraphs: Responsive design adapts an interface's presentation to screen size and interaction methods.
Suppose a desktop layout places data entry on the left and instructions on the right.
On a phone, these areas usually stack vertically.
If the instructions say to check the conditions before submitting, the mobile order must make them available before that action.

blocks.caption: Figure 5 | Change the layout while preserving reading order
blocks.description: Desktop places 2 and 3 side by side; mobile stacks them. Both retain reading order 1→2→3→4. Numbers represent information order, not four actual submissions.

items.title: Desktop
items.body:
1. Task and instructions
2. Data entry
3. Input guidance
4. Check and results

items.title: Mobile
items.body:
1. Task and instructions
2. Data entry
3. Input guidance
4. Check and results

paragraphs: Visual position can change while the meaningful information order remains intact.
WCAG 2.2's Meaningful Sequence criterion requires a correct reading sequence to be programmatically determinable when presentation order affects meaning.
Independent cards need not all have one mandatory order. Check whether reordering changes the intended meaning.

blocks.heading: Field names also need attention
paragraphs: Suppose a text field contains this hint:
“Enter application ID”
This is a placeholder.
It usually disappears when the user starts typing.
A more reliable approach keeps “Application ID” visible as a label and supplies a format example separately.
The code must also associate the label with the input so assistive technologies such as screen readers can identify the control.
Interface design helps people with different abilities and devices understand and operate the service.

sections.heading: 6. Apply the concepts across industries
paragraphs: The following examples identify different content relationships and immediate priorities.

blocks.caption: Information architecture and priorities in six industries
rows: Healthcare
How should patient details, tests, medication and treatment be grouped?
Clinical information needing attention and important warnings
Ecommerce
How should products be classified and filtered?
Price, specifications, stock and purchasing actions
Banking
How should accounts, transfers, investments and loans be organized?
Amount, recipient, transaction confirmation and risk notices
Manufacturing
How should equipment, work orders, maintenance and quality data be organized?
Abnormal equipment, pending work orders and downtime alerts
Education
How should courses, materials, assignments and tests be grouped?
Current progress, the next learning task and unfinished work
Government services
How should applications, lookups, missing-document requests and tracking be classified?
Current case status, deadlines and the next action

paragraphs: These examples share principles, but no fixed layout serves every industry.
A clinical dashboard and a shopping site both need hierarchy. Their requirements for warnings, information density and action restrictions can differ substantially.

sections.heading: 7. Start with a repeatable design process
paragraphs: Turn the concepts into a process that leads from user tasks to a testable interface.

blocks.caption: Figure 6 | From user tasks to a testable interface
blocks.description: Arrows indicate the suggested order of design work. Step five includes validation; drawing a wireframe does not establish acceptance by real users.

items.title: Define users and tasks
items.body: Who will use it? What are they trying to accomplish?

items.title: Inventory content and functions
items.body: Which data, buttons, errors and results are needed?

items.title: Build IA: categories, names and relationships
items.body: Which information belongs together?

items.title: Define states, navigation and visual hierarchy
items.body: What should users notice and do in each state?

items.title: Draw and validate a wireframe
items.body: Check desktop, mobile, keyboard use and real work tasks.

paragraphs: A wireframe uses simple boxes, text and arrangement to show how an interface will work. Detailed icons, color treatment and animation can wait.
Two research methods can provide evidence for the information structure:
Card sorting asks users to group cards labeled with functions or topics according to their own understanding. It explores possible categories in their mental models.

Tree testing starts with a proposed hierarchy and asks people to find an item, such as a parking-permit application. It tests whether they can find the destination without relying on polished visual design.
The first method explores groupings; the second evaluates an established structure.

blocks.heading: Record the result in wireframe-notes.md
paragraphs: Use this simplified template in a practice project:
blocks.code:

paragraphs: The shared project template above retains its original Chinese text in both language editions. The English reading of the template is: 1) User and task: case handler; check whether three required fields are complete. 2) Content inventory: application ID, applicant code, document type, required-field instructions, check action, omissions and corrections, result of the current check, preview and export. 3) Information groups: task and constraints; data entry; check action and results; secondary instructions and diagnostics. 4) Primary action: unchecked—check data; checking—show processing status; missing—fill in and check again; complete—preview and export the current result. 5) Reading order: task → required data → check → result. 6) To verify: do users understand the categories and field names? Are errors explained in text with a correction? Is the mobile reading order sensible? Can the keyboard follow a reasonable order? Are labels programmatically associated with their controls?
This record establishes content, workflow, states and validation conditions before frontend implementation begins.
It also makes requirements clearer when handing the work to a human engineer or an AI coding agent.

sections.heading: 8. Five common mistakes
paragraphs: Use these failure patterns to review a candidate interface.

1. Design an attractive screen before investigating user needs. The resulting workflow may not support the task.
2. Treat IA as menu design. A menu is one way of presenting the information structure.
3. Give all buttons equal emphasis. The primary action becomes unclear and increases the judgment required.
4. Represent errors by color alone. Provide text explaining the problem and how to correct it.
5. Test only the desktop appearance. This misses mobile layout, keyboard use, screen readers and actual operation order.

sections.heading: 9. Check your understanding of M04-03
paragraphs: The three questions appear in the understanding-check section below. Choose an answer yourself before expanding the reference explanation; this page does not submit or save answers.
Organize information first, decide how users will reach it, and then use visual hierarchy to guide attention and action.
Continue with M04-04 on wireframes to turn categories, states and primary actions into a concrete screen plan.

exercise.environment: A text editor and four-state intake sketches, using synthetic field names and data only.
steps: Inventory required fields, actions, states, examples and diagnostics, giving each a purpose and group.
Choose primary actions for unchecked, missing-input and complete states, and identify information that cannot be hidden.
Arrange desktop and mobile versions on paper. Read headings, fields, results and actions linearly and record an ordering question needing implementation testing.
exercise.expected: wireframe-notes.md with a content inventory, groups, primary actions and mobile reading order.
exercise.check: Names are understandable and errors rely on more than color or position. Explain grouping versus navigation appearance.
exercise.cleanup: Keep candidate and pending labels. Do not present personal placement or color preferences as universal tested conclusions.

zh.prompt: 某市政府網站把所有服務按照局處分類，民眾經常找不到申請入口。你認為第一步應該做什麼？
options: 研究民眾的主要任務並重新檢查分類方式
rationales: 側欄顏色不會改變分類關係。
B。先研究民眾要完成的任務與使用的名稱，再檢查分類是否符合他們的理解。深色側欄、放大按鈕或動畫無法直接解決內容放在哪裡的問題；新分類仍需透過尋找任務驗證。
放大按鈕無法決定資訊應放在哪裡。
動畫無法直接修正內容組織。

en.prompt: A government website groups all services by department, and residents often cannot find an application. What should the team do first?
options: Research residents’ main tasks and reconsider the classification
rationales: Sidebar color does not change category relationships.

B. Investigate the tasks residents need to complete and the names they use, then check whether categories match their understanding. Sidebar color, button size and animation do not directly resolve where content belongs. Test the candidate structure through finding tasks.
Larger buttons do not determine where information belongs.
Animation does not directly repair content organization.

zh.prompt: 線上檢查系統顯示資料缺漏，但同時把「匯出」「完成」「檢查」三個按鈕放得同樣醒目。這主要是哪種設計問題？
options: 狀態與視覺優先序不清楚
rationales: 題目沒有資料庫正規化問題的證據。
題目沒有網路效能問題的證據。
C。缺件時應清楚指出缺漏與修正方式，讓「補填並重新檢查」成為目前主要動作。三個動作同樣醒目且沒有條件說明，會讓使用者誤判下一步；題目沒有提供資料庫、網路或字型授權問題的證據。
題目沒有字型授權問題的證據。

en.prompt: A checking system reports missing information but gives Export, Complete and Check equal emphasis. What is the main design problem?
rationales: There is no evidence of a database-normalization problem.
There is no evidence of a network-performance problem.

C. When information is missing, identify the omission and correction, making Fill in and check again the current primary action. Equally emphasized actions without preconditions make the next step ambiguous. The scenario provides no evidence of a database, network or font-licensing problem.
There is no evidence of a font-licensing problem.

zh.prompt: 桌面版把重要說明放在輸入區旁，手機版改成上下排列。設計師最需要額外確認的是什麼？
options: 每張卡片都要完全相同尺寸
手機版一定要有側邊欄
重要資訊與操作的閱讀順序仍然合理
rationales: 相同尺寸不能保證資訊順序正確。
手機是否需要側邊欄要依任務與複雜度判斷。
增加顏色不能保證正確閱讀順序。
D。檢查有意義的內容順序及實際閱讀、鍵盤路徑。使用者應在需要資訊時就讀到它，例如送出前的必要說明。獨立內容可以有多種合理順序；相同卡片尺寸、側邊欄或更多顏色都不是本題的必要條件。

en.prompt: Desktop instructions sit beside a form, but stack vertically on mobile. What particularly needs checking?
options: Every card has exactly the same size
Important information and actions retain a sensible reading order
rationales: Equal sizes do not establish a correct information order.
A mobile sidebar depends on tasks and complexity.
More colors do not establish a correct reading order.

D. Check meaningful content order, actual reading and keyboard paths. Users need instructions when they matter, such as before submission. Independent content can have several reasonable orders. Equal card sizes, a sidebar and more colors are not required by this scenario.
